rule: Every fact, quote, and storyline in a published edition traces to a source registered here, dated at or before the edition's cutoff.
rule_boundary: The rule binds facts, quotes, and storylines. It does not bind authored expression: original metaphor, parody, coinage, humor, and ordinary allusion carry no source requirement. A checkable outside factual predicate asserted inside one still needs admissible pre-cutoff support. See content/editorial-standard.md for the interpretive-warrant ladder governing attributed belief.

source_classes.what: The complete league-data source for the preseason edition, projected from the compiled cutoff-bound edition state: team identities, draft, offseason transactions, historical results, complete cutoff rosters, exact chat quotes with fact_id references. The bundle itself is local private custody (gitignored); the tracked manifest carries edition, cutoff, canonical hash, counts, lineage, and the regeneration command. Writer preflight: python scripts/build_preseason_evidence.py --verify (rejects an absent or hash-mismatched bundle). The preseason writer opens the bundle and contemporaneous coverage, nothing else.

The league's own rules: starting lineup (QB, RB, RB, WR, WR, WR, TE, FLEX, K, DEF, DL, LB, DB), 13 bench, 4 taxi, 2 IR, and the full Sleeper scoring table including IDP. Fetched from the Sleeper API and corroborated as in force before the cutoff by pre-cutoff league chat (PBU=2, solo tackles, the taxi squad, the FLEX, and the move to position-specific IDP slots). This is what makes a lineup argument checkable by a reader; without it the column asserts roster math it never shows.

The league's own power-ranking editions, 2023-2024: eight complete columns written by Karim, Ben, Zach, Patrick, Oscar, Nate and Matt, in five distinct established styles. Read as FORM, not as facts to restate. The Jailyard column is joining a genre these twelve people already run on a rotating weekly author, and a house voice that ignores it reads as an outsider however well written (craft law 28). These are ordinary admitted chat_message facts selected by an explicit fact_id allowlist in scripts/build_preseason_evidence.py, so they carry no special temporal status and quoting their text goes through the ordinary verbatim-quote path like any other chat message.

Weekly data packet: matchups, standings, awards, per-game NFL context (scores, lines, injuries, weather, EPA), all fields derived as-of the edition's week. Weekly editions only; the preseason edition uses preseason_evidence instead.

Sanitized league chat for the edition: verbatim quotes, storylines, and league memory admitted by exact timestamp at or before the cutoff. Weekly editions only; the preseason edition uses preseason_evidence instead.
Franchise records, titles, playoff runs, rosters, draft classes, player arcs. Weekly editions only; the preseason edition uses preseason_evidence instead.
Team identity: roster_id, team name, owner.
Structured editorial decisions accepted by the league (e.g. an accepted ranking order).
Editions already published by this system; the callback surface.

paths: (external; cite URL + publication date in the edition's source notes)
source_classes.what: Outside coverage published at or before the edition's cutoff, cited with its publication date. Primarily NFL articles, reports and takes, and not limited to them: the wider sports world, and news or cultural events a league member would recognize, are admissible on the same terms whenever they bear on the column. Coverage dated after the cutoff is inadmissible. This class registers checkable outside FACTS; the writer's own analogies and allusions are authored expression and need no entry here (see rule_boundary).
